bull.b: The 85% recurring-revenue mix ties a large share of sales to procedures and servicing across the installed base, supporting visibility beyond individual system placements. As utilization and system count expand, instruments and service can compound the company’s revenue base over multiple years.

A 42% operating margin and sharply rising free cash flow demonstrate strong economics and meaningful internal funding capacity. This profitability can support continued research, commercial expansion, customer support, and product development while reducing dependence on external financing.

Expansion of both the installed system base and procedure volumes strengthens Intuitive’s ecosystem and increases opportunities for recurring instruments, accessories, and service revenue. The scale also supports customer familiarity, training infrastructure, and adoption across additional specialties.

bear.b: Slower growth reduces the pace at which Intuitive can expand its installed base, procedures, and recurring revenue streams. Although profitability remains strong, sustained deceleration could limit operating leverage and make future earnings growth more dependent on execution and new indications.

Weak tender activity, local competition, and policy-driven pricing pressure create a structural obstacle in an important international market. Limited placements and the lack of da Vinci 5 clearance in Mainland China may constrain installed-base growth and reduce the market’s contribution.

Extended-use instruments could lower customer cost per procedure in benign cases and reduce instrument-and-accessory revenue per procedure. Because these purchases are a core recurring revenue stream, adoption could pressure monetization even if procedure volumes continue growing.
